I am old now, eighty years, and this small piece of land near my house is what I can still manage. For root crops like cassava and yam, I do not buy chemical fertilizer — the cost is too much and my mother and grandmother grew these same crops without it. I put the household waste and goat droppings on the soil, and I plant the cuttings I saved from last season. My children sometimes come to help me clear the bush, but mostly I work it myself little by little.
